name: table
title: Table
description: One table a document holds: its header and its rows exactly as the document lays them out, with the page and the box it sits in.

files.api/service.yaml:
# THE TABLE'S FUNCTIONS (docs/unoverse/data/objects/README.md 4b). A table is made by no
# function of its own: the pipeline writes it as a part of its document. Its detail is its
# rows, read from its own file in the store (a few kilobytes, never the whole document) and
# filtered here, so an Agent asking
# for the commodities rows gets those and not four hundred others.
#
#   params.where   a phrase: only the rows with a cell containing it, any case
#   params.limit   how many rows at most; 200 when not said
#
# A TABLE THAT IS A PICTURE (2026-09-11, a ROKOS manager review: two tables pasted as images,
# no text in their region) has no rows to read. Its detail renders its region instead, so it
# can be seen; reading the picture into rows is a model's job, not this one's.
getDetail:
  description: The table's header and rows from the store, filtered by params.where and bounded by params.limit.
  input:
    type: object
    properties:
      where:
        type: string
        description: A word or phrase; only the rows with a cell containing it come back (Commodities, Crude, Financials).
      limit:
        type: number
        description: How many rows at most. 200 when not said.
  calls:
    - name: rows
      node: S3FileContent
      when: "return !!row.content.rowsKey"
      config:
        bucket: "{{ row.content.bucket }}"
        key: "{{ row.content.rowsKey }}"
        includeContent: true
    # THE PICTURE KEPT AT READ TIME, for a table read from a picture: the evidence, as a link.
    - name: stored
      node: S3FileContent
      when: "return !!row.content.pictureKey"
      config:
        bucket: "{{ row.content.bucket }}"
        key: "{{ row.content.pictureKey }}"
        includeContent: false
    - name: file
      node: S3FileContent
      when: >-
        return !calls.stored && !!row.content.page && !!row.source_url
          && !(calls.rows && calls.rows.file && (JSON.parse(calls.rows.file.content || '{}').rows || []).length)
      config:
        bucket: "{{ row.content.bucket }}"
        key: "return String(row.source_url).replace(/^s3:\\/\\/[^/]+\\//, '')"
        includeContent: false
    - name: picture
      node: RenderDocument
      when: "return !!calls.file"
      config:
        fileUrl: "{{ calls.file.file.downloadUrl }}"
        fileName: "return String(row.source_url).split('/').at(-1)"
        page: "{{ row.content.page }}"
        box: "return row.content.box ? JSON.stringify(row.content.box) : ''"
        dpi: 150
  returns: >-
    return (() => {
      const t = calls.rows && calls.rows.file && calls.rows.file.content ? JSON.parse(calls.rows.file.content) : {};
      const all = t.rows || [];
      const where = params && params.where ? String(params.where).toLowerCase() : '';
      const hit = where ? all.filter(r => r.join(' ').toLowerCase().includes(where)) : all;
      const limit = params && params.limit ? Number(params.limit) : 200;
      return Object.assign(
        { header: t.header || [], rows: hit.slice(0, limit), total: all.length, matched: hit.length },
        calls.stored && calls.stored.file ? { image: { url: calls.stored.file.downloadUrl, mimeType: 'image/png' }, asPicture: !all.length } : calls.picture ? { image: calls.picture.image, asPicture: true } : {}
      );
    })()
files.props.yaml:
# A TABLE'S FIELDS. Every one is written from the parse by the pipeline, never by the model
# (input: false): the document's make function shapes each table once, and the part writer keeps
# the fields by name (docs/unoverse/data/pipelines/README.md layer 1, parts).
universal_id:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The row's permanent handle, minted from the document's id and the table's own, so a re-read finds the same row.
title:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The table's caption, or its sheet's name, or where it sits and its first columns.
description:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: One line on what the table holds, its size and its columns, so a walk can choose without opening it.
org:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The organisation whose row this is. Assigned by the run.
source_url:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The file the table sits in, the same address as its document.
source_id:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The file's source id, the same as its document's.
partId:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The table's id within its document's structure, such as t5.
page:
  type: number
  input: false
  description: The page the table starts on, counted from 1; for a spreadsheet, the sheet's place.
box:
  type: object
  input: false
  description: Where on the page the table sits, in points with the origin top-left, as x0, y0, x1, y1. Absent for a spreadsheet.
columns:
  type: array
  input: false
  description: The column names, left to right, a multi-row header's levels joined.
  items:
    type: string
rowCount:
  type: number
  input: false
  description: How many body rows the table has.
stitchedFrom:
  type: array
  input: false
  description: The pages of a table continued across pages, stitched into this one.
  items:
    type: number
bucket:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The bucket the document and its structure sit in.
structureKey:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The key of the document's structure in the store, under `_parsed/`, which holds this table's header and place beside the rest of the document.
rowsKey:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The key of this table's own rows in the store, under the document's folder in `_parsed/`, which its detail reads.
whenToUse:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: The question this part answers, as its document's read named it, so a walk can choose it without opening it.
checks:
  type: object
  input: false
  description: How far the table can be trusted. How its rows were read, the share of its cells found in the page text, how many of its totals add up, and why it needs a second look (docs/unoverse/data/documents/checks.md).
pictureKey:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: For a table read from a picture, the key of that picture kept at read time as the evidence, under the document's folder in `_parsed/`, which its detail shows from S3.
files.table.yaml:
unoverse: "1.0"
# A TABLE A DOCUMENT HOLDS (ruled 2026-09-11, docs/unoverse/data/README.md, two levels): rows
# you can filter, sum and compare, found by walking from its document or through a need's
# `of`, never by searching the map. No embed, so it is never positioned; it is a row only
# because a pipeline makes it as a part (`partsOf: document`, docs/unoverse/data/pipelines/README.md
# layer 1, parts). Its rows live in the store, in the document's structure under `_parsed/`;
# the row holds what the table is and where it sits, and getDetail returns the rows.
type: object
name: table
element: content
# THE GLYPH its rows are drawn with (README 4a): a lucide icon name.
icon: table
meta: open

# THE FACE, as a node's node.yaml carries it: what this is and when an Agent reaches for it.
title: Table
description: >-
  One table a document holds: its header and its rows exactly as the document lays them out,
  with the page and the box it sits in.
whenToUse: >-
  Read, filter or compare the figures a document lays out as a table: exposures by sector, a
  fee schedule, a track record, a holdings list, a scorecard. Open it from the document it is
  part of, then ask its detail for the rows that match what you need.
category: Objects
version: 1.0.0

props: { $include: props }
